status_summary: At a UN General Assembly plenary in March 2025 the US Mission stated that the United States rejects the 2030 Agenda and the Sustainable Development Goals (reported by a trade publication on 2025-03-14 and by an April 2025 working paper of the UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network), and a presidential memorandum signed 2026-01-07 directs withdrawal from 66 organizations, including UN DESA, UN-Habitat, the International Tropical Timber Organization and a UN forest-emissions programme. The memorandum does not list FAO, IFAD, WFP, the Committee on World Food Security or the UN Food Systems Summit hub, the Hub's report on the July 2025 stocktake in Addis Ababa does not mention the United States, and a USDA page endorsing the Summit's goals remained readable on 2026-10-12. The general rejection of the 2030 Agenda is operative as a stated position, but the food-specific disengagement the Mandate asks for is only partly reflected, so the record is in_progress at 30.

timeline.event: A trade publication reported that a US Mission counselor told a UN General Assembly session that the United States rejects the 2030 Agenda and the Sustainable Development Goals; an SDSN working paper places the statement at a March 2025 plenary.
The second UN Food Systems Summit stocktake (UNFSS+4) concluded in Addis Ababa; the Hub's report does not mention US participation.

A CRS report stated that the FY2026 request for Contributions to International Organizations was $263.8 million, about 83 percent below the FY2025 pre-rescission level, and that the US had begun withdrawal from WHO and left UNESCO.

A presidential memorandum directed withdrawal from 66 organizations, including UN-Habitat, the International Tropical Timber Organization and the UN-REDD programme; FAO, IFAD and WFP are not among those listed.

title: Remove the U.S. from UN-linked sustainable-development efforts tied to food production
uncertainties: The original US Mission text was not fetched; the March 2025 statement rests on a trade publication and an SDSN working paper (an advocacy-research body), which agree on its substance. A review search for the US Mission's own remarks did not surface them. The memorandum list was read on the Federal Register page in review and confirms that no food or agriculture body other than the International Cotton Advisory Committee and the International Tropical Timber Organization appears. The US role at the July 2025 stocktake was searched and not found. No data on current US funding to FAO, IFAD or WFP were found; the CRS note says the account that traditionally funded voluntary contributions such as WFP's was zeroed in July 2025 and that funding through other accounts is unclear. The USDA 2021 food systems page carries no update date. Whether the withdrawals are intended to reach food production schemes is not stated in the sources. The general withdrawal is covered by c06-03. The SDSN paper is dated April 2025 without a day; 2025-04-01 is a placeholder date.
